chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

There is no thing in which participation is more hateful to me than the pomegranate, and there is no pomegranate except that it contains a seed from Paradise. So when the disbeliever eats it, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sends an angel to him who removes it from him.
ai.seo_question: Why does the Imam dislike sharing pomegranates and what happens to the seed of Paradise when eaten by a disbeliever?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) expresses his dislike for sharing pomegranates due to the belief that each fruit contains a seed from Paradise, which is extracted by an angel if consumed by a disbeliever. This narration highlights the Shia tradition of attributing spiritual significance to natural objects, linking physical sustenance with metaphysical reward and divine judgment.
